gaps.sentence: She was elected ___ president of the students' union.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint/make + role', the article is usually dropped: elected president.

gaps.sentence: We visited ___ Louvre on our last morning in Paris.
gaps.explanation: Most famous buildings and monuments take 'the': the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower.

gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious issue worldwide.
___ sales figures for October look promising.
gaps.explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
gaps.explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).
'Inflation' as a general economic concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ life in the countryside is much quieter.
gaps.explanation: 'Life' in a general sense takes no article: Life is hard sometimes.
